verdict.rationale: iTerm2's own Smart Selection recognizes URLs and file paths in output and opens them with Cmd-click. Semantic History, corroborated by community users, opens Cmd-clicked paths in your editor or the associated app. Copy Mode supports keyboard selection, but no evidence shows a keyboard action that opens a selected URL or path, and users report path formats it misparses or doesn't handle, such as Python stack traces and git diff prefixes. missing for 10: documented keyboard-driven opening of a selected URL or path, robust path recognition across output formats such as stack traces and diff prefixes.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open URLs and file paths from output by clicking them or selecting them from the keyboard

citations.quote: Smart Selection - Quad-click selects semantic objects (URLs, file paths, email addresses, quoted strings). Right-click for context actions. Cmd-click to open.
iTerm2 can perform "smart selection" to highlight URLs, email addresses, filenames, and more by recognizing what is under the cursor
It lets you Command+Click on a path to open it in your editor (or associated application).
Copy Mode - Vim-like keyboard selection. Navigate and select text without touching the mouse.
